Forbairt Eacnamaíoch / Economic Development
NORTH QUAYS
The main river works for the bridge substructure that
includes four permanent concrete river piers, two
concrete bridge abutments and four temporary steel
support frames are complete and are awaiting the arrival
of the bridge superstructure from Ghent, Belgium in April
2025. The pier protection system installation is currently
ongoing upstream of the bridge.   
The fit-out of the bridge superstructure with the
automated mechanical and electrical plant needed for
the opening of the central bridge spans is progressing in
Belgium and the plant room to operate the bridge from
the South Plaza is substantially complete. The
foundations/ pile supported slab for the new public plaza
area on the south quays are in situ and works are now
progressing to raise the ground level.   
The roof of the train station is being completed and
works to the internal layout are also ongoing, including
the first fix of mechanical and electrical works.
Foundations for the northern access point are in place,
this provides access to a pedestrian footbridge and
concourse area over the railway tracks which is
integrated 
The roadworks along Dock Road and Fountain Street
continue to progress under traffic management for the
construction and installation of new footpaths, drainage,
surfacing, services, junctions, lighting, signage and road
markings. New permanent traffic lights at the junction of
Abbey Road and Fountain Street are in operation,
footpaths are also being laid, and greenway access points
are evident, but traffic management continues in
operation for vehicles and pedestrians to facilitate access
arrangements.
Arrangements to start construction works on the railway
flood defence and drainage scheme are currently being
finalised, with works due to commence in early 2025. As
well as constructing flood defence walls, the works also
require significant trackside drainage, underground
impermeable trenching and new pumping stations.
These works are designed to make the existing and new
rail infrastructure climate resilient into the future and
protect it from the increasing impacts of climate change.

The Local Enterprise Office has assisted in the creation of over 1,200 jobs in the 10 years of
its existence and provided over €6.5 million in grant aid to Waterford SMEs. It has trained
over 15,000 employees and hosted over 1,200 training events. Its value to the economy
during the last 10 years is incalculable as its trainers and mentors are predominantly local,
as are the website designers and consultants used for the 872 Trading Online Vouchers
granted to Waterford businesses. The trickle-down effect of this investment in the local
economy cannot be underestimated.
The LEO marked the occasion with an hour of interviews on WLR FM, hosted by Damien
Tiernan. As well as LEO staff members the panel included Mark Bergin of Coffeehouse
Lane, Margaret Fleming of Dessert First, Liam Murray of Marli Products and Stephanie
Wickham of ExPat Taxes.
LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE CELEBRATES IT’S 10TH ANNIVERSARY

County Outdoor Recreation Plan
Work has commenced on the preparation of the County Outdoor Recreation Plan (CORP)
for Waterford. It is an objective of ‘Embracing Ireland’s Outdoors – The National Outdoor
Recreation Strategy’ that each county prepares a CORP and forms a stakeholder grouping
the County Outdoor Recreation Committee. In this regard progress to date has been:
Stakeholder and public consultation will form a key part of the preparation of the plan in
the coming weeks. The project team has invited all councillors to a plenary workshop
regarding the preparation of the plan to be held via Teams on 21st January.
In person public consultation sessions are currently planned to take place as follows:
o  7:30 p.m. Wednesday 29th January 2025 – SETU Arena, Waterford City, X91 XD96.
o  7:30 p.m. Thursday 30th January 2025 – The Park Hotel, Dungarvan, X35 CC97.
o  Online public consultation will also take place around this time.
It is anticipated that the CORP will be finalised by late Q1/early Q2 2025.

Waterford Rural Tourism Network
The Waterford Rural Tourism Network is made up of five cluster areas across Waterford;
Copper Coast, Blackwater Valley, Comeraghs, Gaeltacht na nDéise, and Waterford Estuary.
The aim of the network is to build the capabilities of the individual businesses as well as
enhancing the overall tourism offering in Waterford, this was certainly achieved in 2024. This
year saw the successful delivery of:
3 in person meetings per cluster
2 Network wide events days
2 Learning Journeys – one to the Blackwater Valley and one to the Copper Coast
Online Spotlight Series
This year also saw the launch of the new Visitor Experience Development Programme. This
programme, funded by Fáilte Ireland & facilitated by Runda Hospitality & Tourism Solutions,
will result in further collaboration among the network members and will see the delivery of
new and exciting tourism experiences to the county. 
2025 will see even further developments of the Waterford Rural Tourism Network along with
some unique & interesting meetings and events. To become a member of the Waterford
Rural Tourism Network email Caroline at caroline@runda.ie.

HERITAGE OFFICER REPORT
Waterford Heritage Strategy
Waterford City and County Heritage Forum has prepared a Draft Heritage Strategy covering
the period 2025-2030.The Heritage Strategy sets out strategic objectives relevant to all
aspects of heritage including archaeology, built, cultural, intangible and natural heritage
which will guide annual action plans to achieve those objectives. 10 submissions were
received under the public consultation process and these will inform the final strategy which
will be published in early 2025.
Funding schemes for 2025
The Heritage Organisation Support Fund (HOSF), which provides financial support to not-for-
profit NGOs working in the heritage sector, is now open for applications. 
The Heritage Stewardship Fund, which provides financial support for staff in local authorities,
state agencies and educational institutions with responsibility for heritage programmes, is
now open for applications.
The 2025 Community Monuments Fund is now open for applications until January 31st.
Stream 1 offers grants of up to €100,000 aimed at essential repairs and capital works for the
conservation of archaeological monuments
Stream 2 offers grants up to €30,000 for development of Conservation Management
Plans/Reports/Assessments and detailed Specification of Works that are aimed at identifying
measures for conservation and maintenance of archaeological monuments.
Stream 3 offers grants of up to €30,000 for enhancement of access infrastructure,
interpretation projects and small scale emergency conservation works at archaeological
monuments.Details on www.waterfordcouncil.ie or contact the Heritage Officer directly.

The team is currently addressing a total of 306 properties classified as either derelict or
potentially derelict. In recent weeks and months, there has been a significant increase in
activity, with 97 properties now listed on the Derelict Sites Register. Initial engagement
with property owners or their representatives is crucial for resolving dereliction issues and
gaining insights into the various factors contributing to the properties' current state. 
13
Decade of Commemorations
A Screening of The Aftermath, a film by John Foley and funded by Waterford City and
Council Commemorations Committee  took place in Garter Lane Theatre on November
13th. The Aftermath captures the memories and thoughts of Waterford people talking
about their ancestors involved in the War of Independence and the Civil War. The
documentary film looks at some of the key events and the people involved and also looks
at what happened to those involved in the decades following the period. The film was
funded through the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltact, Sports and Media’s
Decade of Commemorations Fund.  See www.facebook.com/johnfoleyimages for details
of further screenings.
ACTIVE LAND MANAGEMENT AND DERELICT SITES TEAM
The level of activity in the property market concerning vacant and derelict properties has
notably increased. Among the properties we have identified as derelict, several have been
reintroduced to the private market voluntarily, with some currently at the 'sale agreed' or
'to let' stages. We are actively engaging with the new owners of these properties to
ensure they are fully informed of their obligations under the Derelict Sites Act 1990.
Additionally, the introduction of the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant has
contributed to a significant rise in the number of derelict and vacant properties available
on the market at this time.
The table below provides a snapshot of December 2024's activity.

COMPULSORY PURCHASE ACQUISITION OF DERELICT SITES (CPA)
In December, 1 CPA was initiated and publicly advertised. The deadline for submissions
will conclude on the 21st of January 2025. Should there be no objections to this CPA, the
Council will proceed with the vesting process, during which applications for registration of
title will be submitted to the Property Registration Authority. 
In December 2024, the derelict sites team successfully collaborated with property owners
to restore these properties, thereby alleviating their derelict status. Many of these
properties also participated in the Urban Façade Improvement Scheme, administered by
the Economic Development Department.

Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) Grants 2025
Waterford City & County Council has been awarded €219,286 under the Local
Enhancement Programme 2025.  LEP 2025 will launch on 02nd January and will close for
applications at 4pm on January 31st, 2025. Successful applicants will be notified in May
following department approval.
COMMUNITY GRANTS
Age Friendly Waterford in conjunction with Age Friendly Ireland and CARO will host a
Climate Action workshop on January 14th in Central Library lady lane. The workshop will be
followed by a site visit to RENEW social enterprise in Johnstown, Waterford.
AGE FRIENDLY
WELL WATERFORD: ENHANCING HEALTH AND WELLBEING IN WATERFORD
Connecting Communities Roadshows
Final plans are underway to launch the roadshows in early January. Six areas of Waterford
have been identified to host and over 20 partner organisations have committed their
resources and time to be a part of the project again in 2025. In 2024 over 1100 people from
communities attended with a huge effort on collaborative and cooperative working across
sectors. 
This project was shortlisted at the National Chamber awards recently and entered for the
upcoming LAMA awards. 
Healthy Ireland Funding 2025
Several organisations received funding in 2024. The reporting of expenditure and impact is
due back to Pobal and the DOH by February 2025. In January Healthy Waterford will
communicate year 3 of the fund to potential partners who will have a six-week period to
return the application for funding. Budget of €75k which will be delivered in March 2025
on approval of the Well Waterford committee.
Health and Well-being Practitioners Forum (Dec 6)
A successful event took place with over 40 attendees from the Health and Wellbeing
Sector. In 2025 another four of these events are planned along with the monthly meetings
with the Healthy Waterford Coordinator continuing in 2025. 
Playful Communities 
A recent stakeholder meeting reviewed and evaluated this programme. The rebranding
and naming of the project aims to be more inclusive and assure those attending that
more than play takes place. Discussions around identifying specific areas to align with
other stakeholders’ efforts will also be considered. Over 30 events took place in 2024 with a
similar outlook planned for 2025.
Healthy City Accreditation and Interegg Europe Funding 
Unfortunately, our funding application was not successful. However, this application will
be used for future funding opportunities. The WHO Expression of Interest has been
submitted to the WHO with political commitment. Once approved our application phase
will begin in 2025.

The CIFo Working Groups continue to work with agencies and stakeholders to provide
services and supports to all Ukrainians (BOTPs) and International Protection Applicants
(IPAs) residing in Waterford. As of 25th November there are 3,072 BOTPs (increase of 21)
and 621 IPAs in Waterford. Waterford Council teams work with arrivals to the Designated
Accommodation Centre to assist BOTPs under the 90-day protocol to source
accommodation and access services. We continue to seek pledge properties (vacant and
shared) and can be contacted at 058/22059 or offerahome@waterfordcouncil.ie

WATERFORD LOCAL COMMUNITY SAFETY PARTNERSHIP (WLCSP)
WLCSP Update:
The current Coordinators appointed in the National Roll Out of the LCSPs received a
briefing from the Directorate Designate of the National Office of Community Safety
Partnerships. The office is still engaging with the Office of Parliamentary Council and
the Regulations are still a work in progress. A new commencement date for the
Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024 and distribution of Terms of
Reference and Guidance documentation, will be disseminated in due course.  
WLCSP has been engaging with residents/businesses in relation to ASB, vandalism and
bin fires on the Dunmore Road area, in a collaborative ongoing intervention by
Waterford Community Gardai, Waterford City & County Council Departments and

Blue Flag Beach Status
Five Blue Flag applications were submitted to An Taisce’s Blue Flag Beach Unit for Ardmore,
Clonea, Counsellors Strand, Dunmore Strand and Tramore beach for the 2025 bathing
season. The Blue Flag season for beaches in Ireland coincides with the bathing season which
runs from June 1st to September 15th. Blue Flag sites are only awarded for one season at a
time. These Blue Flag sites have been awarded due to their adherence to a strict number of
criteria covering Environmental Information and Education, Water Quality, Safety and
Services and Environmental Management. During the season inspectors will assess each
Blue Flag beach and marina to ensure compliance with the criteria.

The Tom Murphy Litter Competition for Secondary Schools has been judged with prize giving

The Control of Dogs (XL Bully Type Dog) Regulations 2024
The Control of Dogs (XL Bully Type Dog) Regulations 2024 prohibit the importing,
breeding, selling and re-homing of XL Bully type dogs from 1st October 2024. From 1st
February 2025 it will be illegal to own an XL Bully type dog without a ‘Certificate of
Exemption’ issued by the local authority in which the dog resides.
XL Bully owners have between 1st October 2024 and 31st January 2025 to apply for a
Certificate of Exemption. A Certificate of Exemption is issued by the Local Authority and
authorises the owner of an XL Bully type dog to keep that dog at a particular premises
until the natural end of the dog’s life.
This certificate is unique to each XL Bully type dog and owner, and specifies the dog’s
licence details, microchip details, neutering details, age and description. It also specifies
the dog owner’s name, address, date of birth and contact number. 
To date the Dog Control Unit has received four valid applications for a Certificate of
Exemption. All four applications have been approved and issued with a Certificate of
Exemption. 
After 1st February 2025 all XL Bully type dog owners should either be in possession of a
Certificate of Exemption or have proof that they applied for a Certificate of Exemption.
Owners may be required to present their Certificate of Exemption to a Dog Warden or a
member of An Garda Síochána within 10 Days of a request to do so.
Owners can apply, free of charge, to Waterford City & County Council from 1st October
2024 for a Certificate of Exemption through our website, through email or by post.  Further
details are available on our website or at www.gov.ie/xlbully
A further social media and advertising campaign is currently underway to encourage
owners of such breeds to meet their obligations under the regulations.
